goal: Settle the latitude contract for epic-226 (step-lighter, step-back) before wave 1: how much rope the Admiral has, which decisions it may adjudicate vs must surface, checkpoint protocol, budget/model tiers, pre-rulings, and expiry.

questions.question: Which issues are dispatchable and in what wave order?
questions.resolution: Wave 0 = A #227, B #228, C #229, D #230, E #231 (all label 'afk', independently merited, maximally parallel). Wave 1 = F #232, gated on C. G #233 and H #234 carry label 'hitl' and are never dispatched — they are design threads awaiting a human-led explorer pass.
questions.code_evidence: gh issue list --state open (labels afk on 227-232, hitl on 233-234) + issue #226 body 'DISPATCHABLE SET, explicit: wave-dispatch {A,B,D,E} + C, then F after C; G and H are never dispatched'. The C-blocks-F edge is grounded in #232's own acceptance text: 'new tests green in CI (issue C) with zero unexpected skips'.

questions.question: Does any issue rewrite the engine driving this Admiral's own spine (self-hosting hazard)?
questions.resolution: YES. #227 rewrites scripts/checklist_engine.py, which is the live engine driving .agent-work/epic-226/spine.json. fleet-doctrine.md 'Engine/platform quirks' mandates a pre-ruling before wave 1: isolate in a worktree, and before merging verify the new engine drives the LIVE spine read-only (current exits 0) and mutates sanely against a COPY only. #232(a) also touches the same file but is wave 1, strictly after #227 merges, so there is no concurrent-edit collision.
questions.code_evidence: issue #227 body: 'Build, all inside checklist_engine.py'; scripts/checklist_engine.py (93466 bytes) is the engine the epic-226 spine is driven through; skills/admiral/references/fleet-doctrine.md:219-226 (self-hosting-an-engine-edit-mid-run quirk).

questions.question: Is a CI workflow file addable and runnable in this repo (GitHub remote, Actions enabled)?
questions.resolution: The repo has a GitHub remote and is public, and .github/workflows/ does not exist — so #229 is greenfield with no existing CI to conflict with. Runnability was subsequently AMENDED by the human (see q11): Actions minutes are unavailable to this account, so the workflow is authored and verified locally rather than proven by a GitHub run.
questions.code_evidence: git remote -v => https://github.com/fredcai6/constellation-skills.git; gh repo view => fredcai6/constellation-skills PUBLIC; ls .github/workflows/ => No such file or directory.

questions.question: Checkpoint protocol: stop-and-present at every wave boundary, or cleared to run through to closeout?
questions.resolution: Cleared autonomous through wave 0; stop-and-present at the wave-0/wave-1 boundary; then cleared through to closeout (whose own acceptance step remains a human gate).

questions.question: Merge-to-main authority: delegated to the Admiral on green+reviewed, or surfaced per PR?
questions.resolution: Delegated to the Admiral on green tests plus a reviewer APPROVE, merged sequentially and logged. Recorded fallback if the harness permission classifier vetoes gh pr merge: take one human approval in the moment and batch the remaining equivalent merges to the next checkpoint.

questions.question: Model tiers for Commanders and crew, and wave sizing against the shared usage pool?
questions.resolution: Opus Commanders for A #227 and D #230; Sonnet Commanders for B #228, C #229, E #231, F #232; Sonnet crew throughout; no Fable at any tier. All five wave-0 Commanders launch at once, with a 3-then-2 split (A, C, D then B, E) as the fallback if the pool strains.

questions.question: Doctrine and shipped-template edits: may the fleet apply them, or must each be surfaced?
questions.resolution: Delegated when the edit is the one its issue already specifies (A's two global-everyone.md riders, D's planning-template tag convention, E's commander understand paragraph); surfaced if a Commander wants to reshape doctrine beyond its issue. Edits target the canonical skills/_shared/global-*.md, never the regenerated per-role install copies.

questions.question: Scope and honest-null latitude: may a Commander narrow scope or return a measured negative without surfacing?
questions.resolution: Delegated — narrowing scope and returning an honest null are complete deliverables, logged as RULINGs. Adding scope, or dropping an issue outright, is surfaced to the human.

questions.question: When does the contract expire?
questions.resolution: At the wave-0/wave-1 checkpoint, or 24h from confirmation, whichever comes first. Crossing it forces a contract-refresh decision before further dispatch.

questions.question: GitHub Actions availability — does issue C #229's CI actually get to run on GitHub, and if not, what is its acceptance evidence instead?
questions.resolution: Actions minutes are unavailable to this account, so #229 authors the workflow but is NOT expected to prove it via a GitHub run. Its acceptance shifts to local execution of the same command set the workflow invokes (pytest, the coverage floor measurement, the skip-guard), each demonstrated with a seeded failure showing the guard fires. This cascades: PR-2 extends to wave 1 (F #232 also gates on local pytest, not a real CI run), and F's 'green in CI' acceptance reads as 'green under the workflow's own command set, run locally'. The Admiral flagged that a PUBLIC repo normally gets unlimited free Actions minutes, so the cap may be a spending-limit/account setting rather than a true cap; the human's constraint governs regardless.
questions.human_answer: note my github actions are used up, so let's make the ci but only expect it to run locally

signoff.statement: all good go. note my github actions are used up, so let's make the ci but only expect it to run locally — explicit confirmation of the drafted latitude contract as written, with one amendment (q11) folded in: build the CI workflow but expect only local verification. Questioning complete; understanding shared.
